Because for real time proving we need multiple gpus anyway Getting the ELF switching cost should be a quick task, but agree that for production usage we probably don’t want to share a GPU between provers <@577788234810130432> <@412614104222531604> how can I learn more about the testing process? Does the testing process fall in the remit of the pandaops team or who are the teams / stakeholders that I should get in touch with.

excerpts.author: han0110
excerpts.content: It's a new release on upstream that cause Ere script fails, will update Ere tomorrow to fix that

excerpts.author: han0110
excerpts.content:
We can add support of single Ere server instance with multiple ELFs, but it'd require a starting cost when swapping ELF every time.

Sharing the same GPU for multiple Ere servers is doable for ZisK in theory, for other zkvVMs I'd need to check a bit.

excerpts.author: chotuchaiwala
excerpts.content: Are there any tests done around this cost? Also what's special about zisk that it allows for multiple ere servers, should be an interesting read.

excerpts.author: han0110
excerpts.content:
ZisK allows configure the amount of cuda stream to use, configuring it to smaller number would probably allow multiple prover sharing the same GPU (haven’t tested yet tho)

Other zkVMs might also support this kind of config to address GPU with smaller memory

excerpts.author: han0110
excerpts.content: Will try to measure the ELF setup cost and get back here

excerpts.author: taulepton_
excerpts.content: Are you sure we even want to spend time on this?

excerpts.author: taulepton_
excerpts.content: Because for real time proving we need multiple gpus anyway

excerpts.author: han0110
excerpts.content: Getting the ELF switching cost should be a quick task, but agree that for production usage we probably don’t want to share a GPU between provers
